notes: Web search was already used up for the session (200 of 200) before this part began, so nothing here was found by searching. Pages were read directly with the kit's own User-Agent, robots.txt obeyed: the campaign sites the candidates filed with the Secretary of State, governments' own sites (reached from their home pages or site maps), the state DFL's list of endorsed candidates and the University of Minnesota's election archive. A campaign site nobody filed could not be found this way, so a missing website here is not proof that none exists.

The 'website' entries are the addresses already filed with the Secretary of State, recorded here only where the site was opened and names the candidate and the office or place. Not confirmed: cherneyformn.com refused the kit (403) and, read once another way, names only 'Steve Cherney' with no office or district; jamiebarthel.com answered 503 each time.

Out of reach and not worked around: mncourts.gov answers scripts with 403 and mn.gov with a bot check (so nothing for Judge Troy G. Timmerman); Pope County's site returned an empty stub (nothing for Larry Lindor); the search pages of the Andover, Lakeville and New Brighton sites are closed to scripts by robots.txt; Cloquet's school site shows its menus by script.

Read and found not to be sitting members today: Andy Carlson is not on Meeker County's board page (District 1 is Beth Oberg); Mark Reese is not on Lakeville's council page; Jeffrey Nelson is not on New Brighton's; the Kasson-Mantorville, Hutchinson and St. Cloud school board pages do not list Jilaine Rendler, Tiffany Barnard or Steven Schiller (St. Cloud's election page names Steven Schiller as a candidate); the St. Michael-Albertville election page names Brent Harapat as a candidate. Nothing further was found for them, or for Justin R. Anderson (Grant County's directory shows the County Attorney's office without a name in its text) or Nathan Hallgren.

No Republican unit's page could be reached for Karin Housley (Senate District 33) or Steven E. Cherney (House District 58A): the state party's site has no list of endorsed legislative candidates, and the local units' addresses are not known without a search. So no endorsement is recorded for either; that is a gap in the search, not a finding.
Aaron Klemz, own_words: the two words 'Minnesota DFL' are the first entry under the heading 'Endorsements' on his campaign site; the quote is the entry itself, not a sentence.

Reed J. Olson: the election archive's page gives a full birth date and other personal details, which are not recorded (year only, marked secondary, as other parts do). The archive says his county office runs to the present, his own site speaks of it as past; the end year is left blank. His site's Endorsements page shows its content as pictures and was not read.
Shane Richard and Aaron Borchardt: their sites describe careers inside a sheriff's office, which are jobs, not public offices, so no offices are recorded.
Bryan Litsey's site says his campaign is independent of political parties; that is not a party or endorsement statement, so no own_words is recorded.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every address in this file was opened again with the kit's own User-Agent (holmforhouse.com answered 429 once and opened on the second try). All 41 findings were confirmed and none removed. Wording was corrected where the page opened did not show what was written: Karin Housley's 'how' cited a Meet Karin page that was not re-opened (the home page's own sentence is used instead); Reed J. Olson's council entry quoted an About page that now answers 404 (the quote is dropped; the archive's line stands); Bryan Litsey's 'how' cited a City of Chanhassen page with no address given (dropped); John Brillhart's payer line and Aaron Borchardt's site description were reworded to what the pages show; the three DFL entries now give the date the party's page says it was last changed.
